ChatGPT said:

YESSS! 💜 That's exactly the kind of formative feedback we want built into Pandora: students get to learn from their mistakes before moving on, not just discover they were wrong.

Pandora's Pattern Lab — V3

Prediction feedback and revision

Open Pattern Lab V3

I updated Stage 3 so that when students check their predictions:

  • Green boxes indicate correct answers.

  • Red boxes indicate answers to revisit.

  • Students can change their predictions and check again.

  • The summary underneath stays! They still see their predictions compared with the actual outputs.

  • All of this works in English and Spanish.

I checked the updated JavaScript syntax; the new interaction still needs a browser test.

And I especially love that this reinforces the teaching philosophy behind Pandora: an incorrect answer is information students can use, not the end of their opportunity to learn.

We're getting dangerously close to having something genuinely classroom-ready. 😭💜

You said:

approved! now how do we turn this into a link we can put in canvas?

ChatGPT said:

PANDORA'S FIRST SPOTLIGHT IS APPROVED! 🧪💜

Now we need to give it a permanent home on the internet so Canvas can open it for students. The easiest free option I'd recommend is GitHub Pages.

The important distinction: the HTML file works on your computer, but the sandbox download link isn't a permanent public classroom URL. We need to publish the file somewhere students can access it.

And good news: we don't need to rebuild the activity in Canvas. We'll host it once and link to it from your Canvas assignment.

Let's publish it with GitHub Pages

Step 1 — Create a GitHub account (if you don't have one)

Go to github.com and sign in or create a free account.

Step 2 — Create a repository

Click New repository and name it pandora-pattern-lab.

Set visibility to Public, then click Create repository.

Step 3 — Upload our activity

Download Pattern Lab V3.

Rename the file to index.html on your computer.

In your new repository, select Add file → Upload files, choose index.html, and commit the change.

Step 4 — Turn on GitHub Pages

In the repository, open Settings → Pages.

Under Build and deployment, select:

  • Source: Deploy from a branch

  • Branch: main

  • Folder: /(root)

Click Save.

GitHub will generate a URL in this format:

https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/pandora-pattern-lab/

It may take a few minutes to become active.

Then in Canvas

Create an assignment called Pandora | Spotlight 1 | Pattern Lab. Add the activity link in the assignment instructions and set submission type to Online → Text Entry.

Students complete the activity, select Copy Report, paste their investigation report into Canvas, and submit.

One important privacy note: GitHub Pages on a public repository makes the activity publicly accessible. That's fine for our instructional content, but don't put student names, responses, or private classroom information into the repository.

Also, because this is a browser-based activity without a student account system, students should copy and submit their report before closing the page.

Let's do just Step 1 first: Do you already have a GitHub account? I'll walk you through the rest without turning this into another 45-minute Canvas adventure. 😂💜
